2608.15360.title: SAPE: Sandwich Adapters for Parameter Efficiency in Large Language Model Fine-Tuning
2608.15360.paper_summary: While Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) has substantially reduced the hardware cost of adapting Large Language Models (LLMs) by decreasing the number of trainable parameters, recent studies have sought to further improve PEFT through parameter sharing. However, these approaches either employ uniform parameter sharing across layers, which can delay convergence, or rely on dynamic masking strategies, which add computational overhead. The potential of sharing patterns inspired by the inherent hierarchical structure of Transformer architectures remains unexplored in PEFT. To address this gap, we introduce SAPE (Sandwich Adapters for Parameter Efficiency), a PEFT framework based on a sandwich-style hard weight-sharing topology. SAPE routes intermediate Transformer layers through balanced shared group adapters while strictly isolating the input embedding and final projection boundary transformations to prevent gradient interference. This design significantly reduces memory consumption while eliminating the computational overhead associated with dynamic parameter-sharing methods. Extensive evaluations across encoder-only and causal decoder architectures demonstrate that SAPE achieves state-of-the-art performance in low-parameter regimes. On natural language understanding, SAPE outperforms proPETL on RoBERTa-large while utilizing only 10% of the baseline's parameter budget. On natural language generation and world knowledge reasoning with LLaMA-3.2 (3B) under a strict ~0.6M parameter constraint, SAPE outperforms AdaLoRA, yielding absolute improvements of +4.85% on GSM8K and +3.11% on CommonsenseQA. Furthermore, through comprehensive topological ablations, we formalize an inherent capacity trade-off: while hard parameter sharing strongly regularizes semantic generalization, it slightly smooths the sharp layer-wise transformations required for rigid multi-step arithmetic reasoning.
2608.15360.paper_summary_zh: 雖然參數高效微調（PEFT）已大幅降低了適應大型語言模型（LLMs）的硬體成本，透過減少可訓練參數的數量，但最近的研究試圖通過參數共享進一步改善PEFT。然而，這些方法要麼在層之間採用均勻的參數共享，這可能會延遲收斂，要麼依賴動態遮罩策略，這會增加計算開銷。受Transformer架構固有層級結構啟發的共享模式在PEFT中仍未被探索。為了解決這一空白，我們引入了SAPE（參數效率的三明治適配器），這是一個基於三明治式硬權重共享拓撲的PEFT框架。SAPE通過平衡的共享組適配器路由中間Transformer層，同時嚴格隔離輸入嵌入和最終投影邊界變換，以防止梯度干擾。這一設計顯著減少了內存消耗，同時消除了與動態參數共享方法相關的計算開銷。在僅編碼器和因果解碼器架構的廣泛評估中，SAPE在低參數範疇中達到了最先進的性能。在自然語言理解方面，SAPE在RoBERTa-large上超越了proPETL，同時僅使用了基準的10%參數預算。在自然語言生成和使用LLaMA-3.2（3B）進行世界知識推理時，在嚴格的~0.6M參數限制下，SAPE超越了AdaLoRA，在GSM8K上取得了+4.85%的絕對提升，在CommonsenseQA上取得了+3.11%的提升。此外，通過全面的拓撲消融，我們正式化了一個固有的能力權衡：雖然硬參數共享強烈正則化語義泛化，但它稍微平滑了進行嚴格多步算術推理所需的尖銳層級變換。
